pull.title: depends: Update `boost` package to 1.92.0
pull.body:
From the Boost.MultiIndex library [Release Notes](https://www.boost.org/doc/libs/latest/libs/multi_index/doc/release_notes.html#boost_1_92):
> Fixed a performance issue with hashed indices when rehashing at very large container sizes.

Tested ACK 94cb6594573876230840f0c8a563896c8700921b

Debian 13 / GCC 14.2.0.

Independent SHA-256 of `boost-1.92.0-cmake.tar.gz` matches the PR and the GitHub release sidecar:

```
f51707c27359a0df0cac1beada86de31bb5eed5e8285592dadec384df99c2984
```

Tag is `boost-1.92.0` (no `-1` re-release, unlike 1.91.0-1). `BOOST_INCLUDE_LIBRARIES=multi_index;test` still configures. Installed `BOOST_VERSION` is `109200`. The 1.92 hashed-index `reserve_for_insert` floor (`bucket_count()+1`) is in the headers we built.

CMake used the depends 1.92 package (`Boost_DIR=.../depends/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu/lib/cmake/Boost-1.92.0`); `test_bitcoin` compiled `hashed_index.hpp` from `depends/.../boost/include/`.

Both hashed indices (txid, wtxid) live in `CTxMemPool::indexed_transaction_set`. The rehash bug that 1.92 fixes shows up around 50M elements; default `-maxmempool=300` caps the pool in the low millions, more than an order of magnitude below where the float mantissa starts rounding. Still a fine depends bump.

```
make -C depends -j8 boost
cmake -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo -DBUILD_GUI=OFF -DBoost_ROOT=$PWD/depends/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu
cmake --build build -j8 --target test_bitcoin
build/bin/test_bitcoin --run_test=mempool_tests,orphanage_tests,txrequest_tests
```

14 tests, no errors.

Guix builds for the default HOSTS are running; I will follow up with hashes when they finish.

@151henry151 your review comment reads like LLM output. The entire comment could be collapsed into: Checked the hash, did a depends build, and ran the test framework. What is a "GitHub release sidecar"? Please read our [AI policy](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/master/doc/AI_POLICY.md) again.

> when rehashing at very large container sizes.

Note that "very large" here is `200`-`400` million elements (https://github.com/boostorg/multi_index/pull/94#issuecomment-4338298921).

Sorry — my comment was too long, and "GitHub release sidecar" isn't a real thing. I meant the SHA-256 digest GitHub shows next to the release asset, which I compared against the hash in the PR.

The 50M I cited is the first size the multi_index#94 synthetic repro broke; 200–400 million is the production pain in that same thread. Neither is a mempool size.
